title: Building Zemetric's product suite
intro: After Zemetric acquired Evy Energy for its software platform and access to India, I continued as product owner across design and engineering: adapting ChargeConnect for the US market and taking EnergyConnect and FleetConnect from 0→1 to customer pilots over eight months.

sections.heading: Adapting ChargeConnect for US operators
body: ChargeConnect already managed chargers, sessions, payments, revenue, and customer support. The product now had to work for US operators with different payment flows, regulation, utility relationships, and much larger networks.
We rebuilt it on a modern design system, adapted the core workflows, and onboarded US operators including Electrada. Their operating requirements went directly into the roadmap and product releases.

sections.heading: Building EnergyConnect and FleetConnect from 0→1
body: Energy management was for charging operators serving commercial fleets, residential properties, and business sites. Each location had a fixed power limit; crossing it increased costs and reduced charging margins. I led EnergyConnect from 0→1, defining site limits, load schedules, charger groups, and intelligent power allocation.

FleetConnect addressed a different job: keeping vehicles ready for their next route. I worked with fleet teams to turn vehicle telematics, departure schedules, charger availability, and charging priorities into one operating workflow.

sections.heading: EnergyConnect became part of Blink's energy strategy
body: Blink Charging acquired Zemetric in July 2025. It later launched EnergyConnect across 13 Blink-owned DC fast-charging sites in Florida, with phased expansion across the US, UK, and Belgium. Blink described the product as a key part of its long-term strategy to connect, monitor, and manage distributed energy assets across its network.

notes.text: Electrada's fleet program covered 25 sites and 150+ installed high-power DC chargers, substantially larger than Evy's earlier operator base.
EnergyConnect completed 3 customer pilots, including Electrada. FleetConnect reached a successful customer pilot.
Blink Charging (Nasdaq: BLNK) is a publicly listed global EV charging equipment and services company.

chargeconnect.title: ChargeConnect
chargeconnect.description: Adapted Evy's ChargeConnect for the scale and operating realities of US charging networks. The work brought multi-site operations, flexible tariffs, asset health, fault diagnosis, sessions, and revenue into one system so teams could understand and act on network performance.
chargeconnect.caption: Adapted Evy's platform for larger US networks with scalable operations, flexible tariffs, and faster fault diagnosis.

units.caption: Gave CPOs one live view of the network, directing attention to the sites, chargers, and faults affecting service.
Made multi-site operations manageable by keeping ownership, access, and reporting organized around each location.
Created a reliable asset record from commissioning to redeployment, reducing blind spots as charger fleets grew.
Redesigned tariff plans for US clients, supporting flexible flat and dynamic pricing across connectors without configuring each one separately.
Helped operations teams monitor every charging session, including energy delivered, failures, and revenue.
One fault queue combined disconnections, charger errors, failed sessions, and authorization failures for faster support triage.
Created a troubleshooting page that helped operations teams understand asset issues and act on likely causes.
Streamed charger logs directly from hardware and intelligently parsed them so technicians could understand and diagnose issues faster.
Made reliability measurable by separating true downtime from exclusions and exposing the assets lowering network uptime.
Connected utilization to energy and revenue, helping CPOs decide where to fix performance, expand capacity, or reconsider an asset.

energyconnect.title: EnergyConnect
energyconnect.description: Built from 0→1 to help CPOs allocate charging intelligently without breaching site power limits.

units.caption: Gave energy managers early visibility into sites nearing their power limits before constraints affected charging operations.
Connected live demand to site limits so operators could catch overdraw risk before penalties or breaker trips.
Revealed where shared capacity was being consumed across charger groups, making demand peaks explainable instead of opaque.
Pinned demand to individual chargers, helping teams isolate abnormal load and rebalance available capacity.
Used live meter data to adjust charging against actual building demand, protecting capacity shared with other electrical loads.
Translated the site's physical grid setup into enforceable software limits, keeping load decisions grounded in real capacity.
Mapping each charger to its electrical phase let the system distribute demand without overloading one phase.
Let clients choose equal or arrival-based priority, preserve headroom, and keep idle connectors ready to start sessions.
Load groups reserved portions of site capacity for selected chargers while keeping the overall site limit enforced.
Recurring limits reduced charging during grid-constrained or peak-cost hours and restored capacity automatically afterward.
Made every power command traceable from request to charger response, so control failures could be found and verified.

fleetconnect.title: FleetConnect
fleetconnect.description: Built from 0→1 to help fleet operators prioritize charging and keep vehicles ready for departure.

units.caption: Showed vehicle readiness at a glance through driver, charge, range, and priority.
Combined trips, idle periods, and charging into one timeline to explain missed departures.
